definition: One simulated marriage per seed: each year from the wedding the couple may divorce (hazard by marriage duration x couple factors) and each spouse may die (SSA 2023 period life table). The marriage ends at divorce or at the first death; the run follows the couple until both are dead or 100.

sources.1,3: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 21 (NSFG 1995, first marriages): 1-year 0.03, 3-year 0.12 disruption
sources.5,10,20: Copen et al. 2012, NHSR 49 (NSFG 2006-2010, women): first marriage survives 5 years 0.80, 10 years 0.68, 20 years 0.52

after_20.rule: hazard of years 10-20 decays with time constant tau years
after_20.source: assumption: no national data past 20 years; chosen so lifetime disruption stays near the commonly cited 40-50% (PolitiFact 2012 via Wikipedia: Divorce in the United States)

age_at_marriage_25plus.source: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 21: 10-year disruption 0.24 (age at marriage 25+) vs 0.33 total

income_50k_plus.source: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 21: family income $50,000+ (1995 dollars), 10-year disruption 0.23

income_25k_50k.source: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 21: family income $25,000-49,999, 10-year disruption 0.31

births_before_marriage.source: Copen et al. 2012 (NSFG 2006-2010): women with one or more births at first marriage, 20-year survival 0.33 vs 0.52 all

no_births_before_marriage.source: Copen et al. 2012: no births at first marriage, 20-year survival 0.56

parents_intact.source: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 21: intact two-parent family of origin, 10-year disruption 0.29

parents_not_intact.source: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 21: other family of origin, 10-year disruption 0.43

cohabited_before.source: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 21: cohabited before marriage, 10-year disruption 0.40

northeast.source: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 21: Northeast region, 10-year disruption 0.29

he_0_4_older.source: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 21: he is 0-4 years older, 10-year disruption 0.32

remarriage.source: Bramlett & Mosher 2002, Table 41 vs Table 21: second marriages 10-year disruption 0.39 vs first 0.33. No national data for third or fourth marriages: same factor used.

mortality.source: SSA Actuarial Life Table: period life table for 2023, as used in the 2026 Trustees Report. https://www.ssa.gov/oact/STATS/table4c6.html (read 12.11.2026)

ross_rachel.label: Ross & Rachel
ross_rachel.canon: Wedding year 2005 is an assumption (a year after the finale). Ross b. 1967 (Wikipedia infobox; Wikidata 1969), Rachel b. 5 May 1970 (Wikidata). Ross: 3 previous marriages (Carol 1990-94, Emily 1998-99, Rachel 1999). Emma born 2002, before this marriage. Ross's parents married; Rachel's parents divorced. Lived together after Emma. Both high earners in New York.

monica_chandler.label: Monica & Chandler
monica_chandler.canon: Married May 2001 (Wikipedia). Monica b. 1969, Chandler b. 1968 (Wikidata). First marriage for both. Chandler's parents divorced; Monica's married. Lived together before the wedding. No children before marriage.

phoebe_mike.label: Phoebe & Mike

method: Each couple: one marriage per seed from the wedding until divorce or the first death. Divorce hazard by marriage duration fitted to NSFG survival anchors, times the couple's sourced hazard ratios; deaths from the SSA 2023 period life table. Exact counts; 95% Wilson intervals measure sampling only.
